title: Understand
text: The script issues the intake, discovery and research packets in order. The model records what it learns in notes and calls back. It decides nothing about flow.

title: Specify
text: The model writes a spec and a test strategy from the notes, one stage at a time. The script accepts each only after its Improve review, and the spec is committed to docs/shiploop/.

title: Plan
text: The script opens the planning stages. Backchain turns the spec into a dependency graph, and the item's step plan is built the same way. The script, not the model, writes every loop contract and decides when each plan is closed. there is no limit to this

title: Build
text: For each work item the script serves test-spec, baseline, test-author, test-red, implement, test-green and test-refine in order. A revise outcome returns through the script for a replan.

title: Prove
text: Regression, documentation, skill assessment and validation, and static checks each run as a script-served stage with their own result file.

title: Integrate
text: The script integrates verified work and re-verifies the integrated result before the next item.

title: System test
text: The whole product is tested for real against the spec's acceptance criteria, by tests the script requires and checks.

title: Release
text: The script serves the release plan, check, release and verification stages, then operations and handoff, and ends the run with a report.

title: Principles
text: The principles every run is held to. Each reads holds, bent, broken or not examined, worked out from the findings tagged to it and from Claude's review of the run. To change one, tick a change-expectation option in step 3.

title: What we expect of Backchain
text: Expectations for the dependency-planning loop: what each pass should earn, who checks the graph, whether the script uses it, and whether planning is repeated.

title: The script owns the flow
text: The model never chooses the next stage. It does the step in the packet and calls back.

title: The script writes every loop contract
text: Improve, test and quality loop contracts are written by ShipLoop. A model should never size or build one.

title: The packet is the only instruction
text: The model follows the printed packet and commands exactly.

title: One step, then call back
text: Each turn does one stage's work and ends with the exact callback.

title: Evidence is trustworthy and in the repo
text: Findings are committed with the work, and a grade means the engine, not the harness.

title: Behaviour does not depend on the model
text: A pass on the fast gate should predict a pass on a slower, deeper model.

title: Every pass earns its time
text: Each Backchain pass either finds a material gap in the plan or is a confirmation the loop needs to close. Time spent on a pass that finds nothing is the price of closing, and it should be small next to what the earlier passes found.

title: A script verifies the graph
text: Unique step ids, resolved references, one confirmation per produce, no cycles and every step reaching a sink are checked by a ShipLoop script that writes a receipt. The model does not assert them.

title: The script uses the graph to run the work
text: ShipLoop uses the plan graph's order, groups and sinks to open work items and to know when a plan is satisfied. A graph that is only mapped to one item is not being used.

title: Planning is not repeated for the same facts
text: A fact already in the spec, such as the list of acceptance criteria, is not derived again by the model in each loop. The script supplies it and the loops plan only what is new.

title: A closed plan is not revised for visible gaps
text: When Backchain closes a plan, a revise outcome during the build is for what could not be seen at planning time, not for what the spec and sources already showed.
